newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends flat, paring gains as JGBs drop.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends flat, paring gains as JGBs drop.

text.p: TIFFE key September three-month Euroyen futures on Friday ended unchanged from the day before, shedding their morning gains in the afternoon in sympathy with a sharp fall in Japanese government bond futures, traders said.
The September rose in the morning session on short covering, they said.
Those who bought back in the morning reverted to selling in the afternoon as JGBs tumbled, a city bank trader said.
The key March JGB futures contract ended at 124.41, down 0.54 from Thursday's 124.95.
Bond traders said investors sold cash JGBs and non-JGB issues to lock in profits and cover losses from Tokyo's sagging stock market.
In the Euroyen market, however, the stock market's woes were also considered a supportive factor, by suggesting that Japanese interest rates are likely to remain low.
The consensus in the market is that weak Tokyo share prices will prevent the Bank of Japan from guiding short-term interest rates higher, the city bank trader said.
In the Tokyo stock market on Friday, the Nikkei 225 settled 77.46 points or 0.40 percent higher at 19,369.04, bouncing only lightly from sharp losses earlier in the week.
The Bank of Japan injected 500 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining its neutral stance.
The key overnight call rate was heavily traded at 0.48 percent, a trust bank trader said.
